focus: Angle 1 at the shape layer — do the record and field shapes each plan assumes match the runtime's actual types, and do the new fields have a named home?
noveltyJustification: All three findings are new: the memory-proposal bot contradiction against holdForBot, the unnamed proposal item fields, and the by/actor naming split in phase 001's plan description.
keyQuestions: Plan versus runtime: do the files, functions, records, fields and verbs each plan names exist with the shapes it assumes, and are its test and verify commands runnable here?

graphEvents.label: Memory-proposal item contradicts itself on the proposing bot
Phase 001 run-record field named by in the plan description

label: Phase 005's memory-proposal item contradicts itself on the proposing bot: REQ-007 says it carries the proposing bot, REQ-008 appends to that bot's file, and REQ-009 says it holds no bot so holdForBot ignores it. holdForBot selects by botId and open state with no kind check, so either the item carries the bot id and holds the bot, or it carries none and the confirm path cannot find the file. Give the item a proposalBotId and a kind of memory-proposal, and make holdForBot and itemAwaitingResume skip that kind.

Phase 005's REQ-007 names no item field for the type, the fact or the bot, while the plan's rollback note refers to an item carrying kind; the NeedsYouItem validator is an explicit key list, so an unnamed field cannot be added. Name the keys (kind, memoryType, fact) in REQ-007 and add them to the needs-you.ts file-table row and the ITEM_KEYS change.

Phase 001 calls the run-record field by: in its plan description and actor everywhere else, and never names its field group. RunRecord is eight named groups, and a top-level actor sits outside all of them. Change the description to actor and name the group (identity or request) in REQ-005 so the validator, index column and JSON reader agree on one path.

direction: Treating RunSummary's new fields as unnamed
reason: Phase 004 REQ-005 names lastRun.branch and lastRun.worktreePath in the JSON, and the data already exists in EvidenceLocations.branch and worktreePath, so the phase surfaces it without a new record field.

direction: Treating the BotDefinition key additions as a collision
reason: FRONTMATTER_KEYS holds thirteen keys today and the four phases that add one each add a distinct key: routine, memory, apps, skills; phase 008 adds none because secrets already exists as Posture.secrets.

direction: Treating HonoredPosture as an open key bag
reason: The record validator checks group presence and named fields and never enumerates posture keys, so 007's and 008's additive fields need no validator change.

direction: Treating the needs-you key list as automatically extensible
reason: ITEM_KEYS is an explicit array, which is why phases 001 and 006 both say they update it and why the unnamed 005 fields matter.
